LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Ancient Greece
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An introductory historical archive describing the Greek city-states, their wars, political experiments, culture, religion, and intellectual life.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Roman Empire
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A surviving historical record of Rome's transformation from republic to empire, its government, military expansion, society, and long influence on later civilizations.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Qin and Han China
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A historical record describing the unification of ancient China under Qin, followed by the political, military, administrative, and cultural development of the Han dynasty.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Industrial Revolution
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An account of the transformation of production, transportation, urban life, labor, and economic organization during Earth's industrial age.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Second World War
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A historical account of the global war fought from 1939 to 1945, including its major powers, military campaigns, mass destruction, ideological conflicts, and consequences for the old Earth.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Cold War
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A record of the long geopolitical and ideological rivalry between competing power blocs after the Second World War, including nuclear deterrence, proxy conflicts, technological competition, and political division.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Introduction to Plato
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A philosophical archive introducing Plato's thought, including questions of justice, knowledge, virtue, political order, education, and the nature of reality.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Introduction to Aristotle
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A philosophical archive introducing Aristotle's writings on logic, ethics, politics, causation, nature, virtue, and the pursuit of human flourishing.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Stoic Philosophy
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A collection of ideas associated with the Stoic tradition, emphasizing virtue, reason, self-command, acceptance of what cannot be controlled, and responsibility for one's own judgments.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Enlightenment
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An archive introducing the early modern intellectual movement that emphasized reason, criticism of inherited authority, natural rights, scientific inquiry, and debates over political legitimacy.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Introduction to Immanuel Kant
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A difficult philosophical archive introducing Kant's investigation of human knowledge, moral obligation, freedom, reason, and the limits of metaphysical speculation.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Hebrew Bible
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An introductory archive describing the collection of ancient Israelite scriptures concerning creation, covenant, law, kingship, wisdom, prophecy, worship, exile, and hope.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Introduction to Christianity
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An introductory record of Christianity, including its origins in ancient Judaism, belief in Jesus Christ, the early Christian movement, scripture, worship, salvation, and major themes of Christian teaching.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Life and Teaching of Jesus
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A surviving record introducing Jesus of Nazareth, his teachings, relationships, public ministry, crucifixion, and the Christian claim that he rose from the dead.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Early Christian Church
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A record of the development of early Christian communities, their missions, persecutions, theological disputes, councils, worship, and growth throughout the Roman world.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Protestant Reformation
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A historical and theological archive describing the sixteenth-century reform movements that challenged Western church institutions and reshaped Christian theology, worship, politics, and European society.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Ancient Political Thought
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An archive surveying ancient debates about law, justice, citizenship, monarchy, aristocracy, democracy, political virtue, and the proper organization of human communities.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Republican Government
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A political archive discussing systems in which public authority is understood as belonging to a political community rather than to a hereditary ruler, including institutions, representation, civic virtue, and constitutional limits.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Liberal Political Thought
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An archive introducing political traditions concerned with individual liberty, legal equality, rights, constitutional government, private judgment, and limits on political authority.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Socialist Political Thought
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An archive introducing political and economic traditions critical of social inequality and concentrated private ownership, including debates over labor, class, collective ownership, planning, democracy, and social welfare.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Modern Nation-State
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A political archive describing the development of territorial states, nationalism, citizenship, sovereignty, bureaucracy, diplomacy, borders, and centralized political institutions on old Earth.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Scientific Revolution
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An archive describing the transformation of Earth's understanding of nature through observation, mathematics, experimentation, astronomy, mechanics, and new methods of scientific inquiry.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Biological Evolution
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A scientific archive introducing the theory that populations of living organisms change across generations through processes including variation, inheritance, natural selection, and common descent.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The Rise of Computing
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A technological archive tracing the development of electronic computing, digital information, programming, networks, and increasingly powerful machines during the final centuries of old Earth civilization.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: The First Age of Spaceflight
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: An archive describing humanity's first journeys beyond Earth, including rockets, satellites, crewed spaceflight, lunar exploration, orbital stations, and the beginnings of interplanetary ambition.

LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.title: Artificial Intelligence on Old Earth
LiAIChat.Archive.ArchiveContentDef.summary: A surviving archive describing old Earth's attempts to construct machines capable of learning, reasoning, generating language, recognizing patterns, and performing tasks once associated with human intelligence.
